Understanding the Procedure

What Is a Sinus Lift?

A sinus lift — also known as sinus augmentation — is a procedure used in implant dentistry to increase the amount of bone available in the upper jaw. It is carried out when the natural bone height beneath the sinus cavity is insufficient to support dental implants.

During the procedure, the sinus membrane is carefully lifted and bone graft material is placed beneath it. Over time, this material encourages new bone growth, increasing the height and volume of bone available in the upper jaw to support stable implant placement.

The procedure is a well-established part of implant treatment planning and is considered when the upper back teeth — the premolars and molars — need to be replaced with implants but the available bone is not sufficient in its current state.

When the Procedure Is Considered

Why a Sinus Lift May Be Needed Before Dental Implants

Several factors can lead to insufficient bone height in the upper jaw. Bone loss commonly occurs after tooth extraction, as the jawbone gradually resorbs when it is no longer stimulated by a tooth root. The longer a tooth has been missing, the greater the degree of bone resorption that may occur.

In the upper jaw, the sinus cavity sits directly above the roots of the back teeth. When these teeth are lost, the available bone between the sinus and the top of the jaw ridge may not be deep enough to accommodate an implant of sufficient length.

Some patients naturally have a larger sinus cavity or thinner bone in this area, which can further limit the available bone height. A clinical assessment, including imaging, is carried out to evaluate bone dimensions and determine whether a sinus lift is required before implant placement.

Bone loss after extraction
Limited upper jaw bone height
Long-term missing teeth
Supporting Stable Implant Placement

How Sinus Lift Procedures Support Implant Placement

The purpose of a sinus lift is to create sufficient bone support in the upper jaw so that dental implants can be placed securely. By increasing the bone height beneath the sinus cavity, the procedure provides a stable foundation for implants that would not otherwise be possible.

Bone graft material is placed beneath the sinus membrane, where it acts as a scaffold for new bone growth. Over the healing period, the body gradually replaces the graft material with natural bone, increasing the available height and volume.

Once sufficient bone regeneration has been confirmed through clinical review, implant placement can proceed with greater confidence that the implants will have the support they need to integrate successfully with the surrounding bone.

The Treatment Process

The Sinus Lift Procedure Process

The sinus lift process follows a carefully planned sequence of stages, each tailored to your individual clinical needs and circumstances.

01

Clinical Examination & Assessment

A thorough examination of your upper jaw, including imaging, to evaluate bone height, sinus anatomy, and overall suitability for the procedure.

02

Treatment Planning

A personalised treatment plan is developed, outlining the approach, expected healing period, and how the sinus lift fits within your wider implant treatment.

03

Bone Graft Placement

Bone graft material is carefully placed beneath the sinus membrane under local anaesthetic. The membrane is gently lifted to accommodate the graft material.

04

Healing & Bone Regeneration

A healing period follows to allow the graft material to integrate and new bone to develop. Progress is monitored through review appointments.

05

Planning Implant Placement

Once sufficient bone regeneration is confirmed, planning for implant placement can proceed, completing the preparation for your implant treatment.

Recovery & Healing

Healing After a Sinus Lift

Following a sinus lift, a healing period is required to allow the bone graft material to integrate and new bone to regenerate. The length of this period varies between patients and depends on individual healing capacity and the extent of the procedure.

During the healing phase, your clinician will schedule review appointments to monitor progress and confirm that bone regeneration is proceeding as expected. It is important to follow the aftercare guidance provided to support the healing process.

Implant placement may follow once your clinician has confirmed that sufficient bone support has been achieved. For patients with missing teeth in the upper jaw, the sinus lift is an important preparatory step that helps ensure the long-term stability of the implant restoration.
